- When sentiment is positive (≥0.25) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.25) and forecast is falling, avoid excessive downward bias — adjust downward only if confirmed by recent price action.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast peak height and slow decay.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.20) and forecast is trending, apply mean reversion bias — forecast should not drift beyond 1.5x recent 7-day average.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >10% from forecast in first 5 days, adjust forecast to align with recent 10-day moving average.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “highs” followed by “low” sentiment, forecast should be capped at 1.2x prior peak to avoid over-leverage.  
- When sentiment is high (≥0.50) and forecast is flat or declining, reverse direction — model may be underestimating bullish momentum.  
- If forecast is consistently above true outcome by >5% over 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day to avoid “over-forecasting” bias.
